claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have a son, Alex, who's 17. I live here in the UK and he lives at home with me. I'm just trying to figure out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know that Alex is 17 and lives with you here in the UK.

To determine Alex's eligibility, I need to understand his current situation regarding education or training. Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 17 and studying for his A-levels, I need to clarify one more important detail.

When did Alex turn 17, or when will he turn 17? I need to know his date of birth or at least which month and year he turned/will turn 17, as this affects eligibility rules for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, he turned 17 earlier this year, back in March.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex turned 17 in March of this year and is currently studying for his A-levels (which is full-time non-advanced education), I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Is Alex enrolled to continue his A-level studies beyond his 20th birthday, or is he expected to complete them before then?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he'll finish them well before he turns 20. He's doing a standard two-year A-level course, so he should be done by the time he's 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very helpful. Just a couple more questions to ensure I have all the information needed.

Are you the person responsible for Alex? By this I mean, are you the one who is primarily responsible for him and he lives with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. I'm his parent and he lives here with me. I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. One final question: is there anyone else who might also be claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as another parent or guardian?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why: Alex is 17 years old and currently studying for his A-levels, which qualifies as full-time non-advanced education. Child Benefit can continue for young people aged 16 to 19 if they remain in approved education or training. Since you are Alex's parent, he lives with you in the UK, you're responsible for him, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him, you meet all the eligibility criteria.

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex until he finishes his A-levels or turns 20, whichever comes first (in his case, he'll finish before turning 20).

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
